person.name: Bruno Moya
person.headline: AI engineer & technical founder · CTO at TopBrokers · Founder at Glassear
person.tagline: I turn emerging technology into real products.
person.seoTitle: Bruno Moya | AI Engineer · CTO at TopBrokers · Founder at Glassear
person.description: Software engineer and technical founder based in Barcelona. Builds agentic AI systems that run in production: CTO at TopBrokers, where LLM and messaging workflows handle over 1,000 conversations a day, and founder of Glassear, whose Studio platform turns natural language into interactive XR applications. A decade of hardware, computer vision and infrastructure underneath.

positioning.intro: I started programming at 13. In 2015, still a teenager, I started building Glassear because I wanted AR glasses I couldn't buy. Glassear needed hardware, so I learned hardware; it needed computer vision, so I learned computer vision. Later came backend, infrastructure and AI. The technologies changed; the habit didn't: pick a hard problem, build it, break it, understand why, and build it again until it works outside a demo.
positioning.principle: I turn emerging technology into real products.

principles.title: AI should do things, not just talk about them.
principles.body: It gets interesting when a model can use real tools, change a real scene or call a real API, with deterministic checks around it deciding what actually happens.

principles.title: The prototype is where the real work starts.
principles.body: Making something work once is a demo. Making it work on an ordinary Tuesday, for someone else, with bad Wi-Fi, is a product.

principles.title: I like owning the whole problem.
principles.body: Frontend, backend, hardware, AI or infrastructure are implementation choices. If it's part of the product, it's part of the problem.

principles.title: Emerging tech gets interesting when it stops feeling emerging.
principles.body: AR and AI don't matter because they're new. They matter the day a musician reads a score hands-free, or a team stops doing something by hand.

experience.summary: Hands-on technical ownership of an AI- and automation-driven real estate technology platform, from architecture and implementation to deployment and operations.
highlights: Architect and build backend systems, APIs, automation platforms and distributed services.
Operate PostgreSQL, Docker, Linux, networking, backups, monitoring and cloud/on-premise infrastructure.
Design fleet and device management, browser/device automation and communication workflow systems.
Lead infrastructure migrations and optimization work focused on reliability and cost efficiency.
Make architecture decisions and deliver production systems as both technical leader and hands-on engineer.

experience.summary: Founded Glassear in 2015 and kept iterating the device for a decade across optics, mechanics, electronics and software. Glassear now builds an AR / spatial computing ecosystem: Glassear One hardware, the Glassear Studio platform and GlassMusic.
highlights: Glassear One: optical see-through AR headset that uses the user's smartphone as display and compute, avoiding video passthrough and reducing cost, weight and proprietary electronics. Patent pending.

Build Glassear Studio, an AI-native platform that turns natural-language intent into interactive spatial applications: Unity integration, own runtime, GLX, scene patches and revisions, runtime synchronization, AI Planner, Intent Graph and agent tooling.
GlassMusic: first vertical use case, hands-free AR for music learning and performance; shown at 4YFN/MWC 2025 and pitched at 4YFN/MWC 2026 from the Catalan Arts stand.
Selected for the ACCIÓ Catalan Pitch Competition 2025 catalogue of 50 Catalan startups with the most potential.
Own product direction, architecture and implementation across hardware, Unity, TypeScript, React, Node.js, Python and PostgreSQL.

experience.summary: Built the Hess Test web application for psychological evaluation in recruitment, with a React interface and a WordPress/PHP backend.
highlights: Implemented data storage, user management and automated email delivery.
Used processing queues to run reliably within shared-hosting constraints and supported multiple devices and browsers.

experience.summary: Supported FECAMM, a rare-disease non-profit, in bringing accessible games to the Patient73 platform.
highlights: Helped organize month-long game jams with UAB, UPC and participating hospitals.

experience.summary: Built and optimized AR applications and interfaces using ManoMotion hand tracking, Unity and computer-vision techniques.
Developed an Android application in Java for pose, face and object tracking during an internship at the Computer Vision Center.

projects.name: JobAgent
projects.title: JobAgent - Autonomous AI Job Search & Application System
projects.outcome: I use JobAgent to manage my own job search.
projects.problem: Job discovery and application management combine semantic judgment with workflows that must remain accurate, traceable and under candidate control.
projects.description: An autonomous, agentic job-search platform for role discovery, semantic matching, job analysis, CV tailoring and controlled browser-assisted applications.
projects.architecture: FastAPI and Celery services coordinate PostgreSQL-backed workflows with a React/TypeScript interface and Docker deployment. The application lifecycle is represented as an explicit state machine with observability and audit trails.
projects.aiComponent: LLMs analyze role fit, tailor CV content and support agent workflows through an OpenAI, Anthropic and Gemini abstraction. Reactive Resume is integrated through REST and MCP.
projects.deterministicComponent: Playwright automation, approval gates, the Candidate Answer Vault, application state transitions and anti-hallucination safeguards keep actions repeatable and reviewable.
projects.principle: LLMs are used where semantic reasoning is useful; deterministic software is used where reliability, integrity and repeatability matter.
highlights: Multi-source job discovery
Semantic job matching
Human-in-the-loop approval
Telegram notifications
Observability and auditability
projects.story: I got tired of searching for jobs manually, so I started building an agent to help me do it.

projects.name: TalentGapAnalyzer
projects.title: TalentGapAnalyzer - AI Workforce Intelligence
projects.problem: Organizations need a defensible way to understand skill gaps, role compatibility and workforce development opportunities.
projects.description: AI-powered workforce intelligence and talent gap analysis platform built as a team project at UAB The Hack 2025.
projects.architecture: A Python/FastAPI analysis backend uses Pandas and Scikit-learn, with a React interface, provider fallback, caching and cost/token tracking.
projects.aiComponent: OpenAI, Anthropic and Gemini generate career recommendations, development plans, organizational insights and explainable narratives.
projects.deterministicComponent: Structured compatibility analysis, caching, cost tracking, bias checks, guardrails and audit data constrain and explain generated output.
projects.principle: Model-generated recommendations are paired with measurable analysis, safeguards and explainability.
highlights: Employee skill-gap analysis
Employee/role compatibility
AI-generated development plans
Bias detection and guardrails
Multi-provider fallback
projects.story: We had a hackathon, a problem worth solving and very little time. We built TalentGapAnalyzer and it won UAB The Hack 2025.

projects.name: Glassear Studio
projects.title: Glassear Studio - Natural Language to Interactive XR
projects.outcome: An AI-native platform for building and modifying interactive XR applications across a web authoring environment and Unity runtime.
projects.problem: Creating interactive XR applications normally requires specialized tooling and manual coordination between authoring systems and runtime state.
projects.description: Glassear Studio translates natural-language intent into structured, synchronized changes to interactive XR applications.
projects.architecture: An AI Planner and Intent Graph coordinate tool-based operations, MCP integrations, structured scene patches and runtime synchronization between a TypeScript/React/Node.js web platform and Unity.
projects.aiComponent: LLMs interpret intent and plan tool calls within explicit system constraints.
projects.deterministicComponent: Typed operations, validation, reconciliation and runtime acknowledgements control how planned changes become scene state.
projects.principle: Reasoning proposes changes; deterministic contracts validate, apply and synchronize them.
highlights: Natural-language-to-application workflows
AI Planner and Intent Graph
Agent and MCP tool architecture
Structured scene/runtime modifications
Hybrid deterministic and LLM architecture
projects.story: Creating spatial apps is still slow and specialised. Glassear Studio makes it closer to describing what you want and letting AI agents help build it.

projects.name: MapAnim
projects.title: MapAnim — Route Motion Studio
projects.outcome: An interactive route-animation editor combining itinerary editing, camera controls, map styling and a frame-by-frame export pipeline.
projects.problem: Turning a travel itinerary into a map animation requires coordinating route geometry, camera movement, timing and video rendering.
projects.description: A browser-based editor for animated travel maps, with an editable itinerary, camera controls, a timeline, map styles and MP4 export.
projects.architecture: React and TypeScript power the editor, MapLibre GL renders the map, and Zustand manages project state. A shared scene engine evaluates the route and camera at a given time. Playwright captures frames in Chromium and FFmpeg encodes the video.
projects.aiComponent: The route animation and video export pipeline does not depend on generative AI.
projects.deterministicComponent: The editor preview and frame-by-frame export share getSceneAtTime(project, time), so both use the same route and camera calculations.
projects.principle: One scene model for interactive preview and exported video.
highlights: Editable itineraries, GPX import and route timing on a timeline.
Camera controls and continuous route transitions.
Multiple map styles and a Route 66 example from Chicago to Santa Monica.
Frame-by-frame capture and FFmpeg MP4 encoding.
projects.story: Bringing geospatial rendering, camera choreography and video export together in an interactive creative tool.
